question: How do you answer range sum queries with point updates fast? Explain Fenwick trees and segment trees.

scenes.sub: Range queries with updates, in O of log n each.
scenes.say: Range query problems say: here's an array. Answer sums or minimums over ranges, while values keep changing. Fenwick trees and segment trees both do that in log n.

scenes.head: The problem: n = 8, many queries and updates
scenes.say: Take eight numbers. A plain array updates in one step, but a sum scans up to eight cells. Prefix sums answer a sum in one step, but one update must rewrite up to eight. With two hundred thousand queries on a big array, linear cost is too slow. The fix is a tree of subtotals, where both operations cost about log n. For eight cells, that's three steps.

scenes.head: Fenwick: sum of the first 7 values
scenes.say: Array: three, two, five, one, four, six, two, seven. The Fenwick tree stores, at position i, the sum of the last lowbit of i values. Position four covers one to four. Position six covers five to six. To sum the first seven, start at seven: two. Remove the lowest set bit of seven to drop to six: ten, total twelve. Remove the lowest bit of six, then four: eleven, total twenty three. Three steps, not seven.

scenes.head: Fenwick tree in code
scenes.say: Query goes down: subtract the lowest bit each time, adding tree values. Update goes up: add the lowest bit each time, changing every cell that covers position i. Both loops run at most log n times. A range sum is sum of r minus sum of l minus one. It's tiny, which is why contest people love it. Its limit: it needs an operation you can subtract, like sums.

scenes.head: Segment tree: also min, max, and more
scenes.say: A segment tree stores the array's values as leaves, and every parent holds the combination of its two children, here a sum. Update: change a leaf, then recompute the parents up to the root. Query: walk inward from both ends of the range, taking whole blocks. Swap the plus for min or max and it works unchanged. Range updates need lazy propagation, the usual follow-up. Time is O of log n per operation.

scenes.head: In the interview
rows: Fenwick for prefix sums, shorter code. Segment tree for min, max, or lazy updates.
Fenwick: n adds, n log n. Segment tree: O of n.
Cell i covers exactly the last lowbit of i values.
Fenwick is 1-indexed; index zero loops forever.
scenes.say: Follow-ups. Fenwick or segment tree? Fenwick for sums, a segment tree for min, max, or lazy range updates. Build time? Segment tree is linear. Why lowbit? Cell i covers the last lowbit of i values. Classics: Range Sum Query Mutable, Count of Smaller Numbers After Self. The common mistake: using index zero in a Fenwick tree. It loops forever.

lines: Both answer range queries with point updates in O of log n.
Fenwick: tiny, for sums. Segment tree: general, supports min, max, lazy.
Index from one in a Fenwick tree.
scenes.say: Both answer range queries with point updates in log n. Fenwick is tiny and made for sums. A segment tree is general, and supports min, max, and lazy updates. And remember to index from one in a Fenwick tree.
